_comment: The cross-CLI verb-set contract (issue #570, epic #361). tools/check_cli_verb_parity.py
runs each shipped `ball` CLI's --help, extracts its verb set, and checks it against this
file. Editing this file is how a verb-set difference gets ACCEPTED — deliberately, in a
reviewed diff — instead of drifting silently, which is exactly what happened to Go and
Python: #361's 'every registry's ball exposes the uniform verb set' lived only in prose.
portable  the verbs every `ball` must expose. Adding one here fails every CLI that has
not shipped it yet — that is the point.
ignore    pseudo-verbs a CLI may list in its Commands block that are not real verbs.
clis[x].extras    verbs this CLI exposes BEYOND the portable set, each an accepted
target-specific surface. An undeclared extra fails the check.
clis[x].missing   portable verbs this CLI does NOT expose yet, with a reason. A missing
entry that is no longer missing also fails, so the carve-out cannot

dart.reason: Dart is the reference CLI and predates `check`; its `validate` covers the same ground (dart/cli/lib/src/runner.dart's _validate). The registry verbs (init/add/resolve/publish/build) and round-trip are Dart-only by design — no other target ships a package registry.

ts.reason: ts/cli ships the execution + report verbs only; @ball-lang/compiler and @ball-lang/encoder are consumed as libraries rather than through the CLI (ts/cli/AGENTS.md). `audit` is shared with Dart, whose analyzers self-host (#362).

rust.reason: Full portable surface since #365; `audit` is shared with Dart/TS.
